item.title: ClaudeDeck 0.3.0
item.description:
ClaudeDeck 0.3.0 adds usage limits, git history and branches, a GitHub inbox, history search, Skills and a live view of each session's agents.

New

  • Claude usage meter. Your plan's 5-hour and weekly usage with reset countdowns, under the sidebar and in the menu bar. When a session stops on the usage limit, ClaudeDeck sends it "continue" once the limit resets (Settings › Sessions to turn off).
  • Agents panel (⇧⌘A). A third tab next to Files and Changes that follows the session you're on: the subagents it started (type, task, status, duration, tool calls, tokens), a 30-minute timeline and a live activity log.
  • Branches, History and Worktrees. A branch picker on the Changes header (switch with Stash & Switch, create, check out remote branches), a commit graph in a History tab, and a Worktrees page to see which session uses which worktree, open, remove or prune them.
  • GitHub Inbox. Open issues and pull requests of the project's repo; Start Work opens a Claude session linked to the item.
  • Fix CI with Claude. Failed checks of a linked pull request can be sent — with the failing log — to Claude in one click.
  • Automations on GitHub events. Trigger an automation when a new issue or pull request appears (optional label/author filter).
  • History search (⇧⌘H). Search every Claude conversation; double-click a result to continue it.
  • Skills. Browse, preview, edit and create your user, project and plugin skills.

Fixes

  • Clicking a session in the sidebar (or ⌘J, or the waiting tray) puts the keyboard focus in its terminal right away.
  • "Continue where you left off." no longer stays unsent in the input while Claude is still starting up.

Installed 0.2.x? This update arrives through ClaudeDeck › Check for Updates… (or on its own within a day).

item.title: ClaudeDeck 0.2.1
item.description:
A calmer sidebar that doesn't move under your cursor, and ⌘-click for bare file names.

Sidebar

  • Rows stay where they are. Status changes no longer reorder the list; a project's state shows in place. Changes the app makes on its own (a project becoming active, automations, iCloud sync) wait while the pointer is over the sidebar and briefly after a click, so you don't click the wrong project.
  • "Waiting for you" tray. Sessions that need you — permission prompts, questions, freshly finished turns — slide up in a tray at the bottom of the sidebar, with Allow / Deny right there. The list above doesn't shift.
  • Compact rows. A project with a single session takes one row instead of two.
  • Quieter idle. Sessions you've already looked at show a grey dot instead of a yellow "Your turn" pill; the pill is only for turns you haven't seen.
  • Group badges. Group headers show how many sessions are waiting (red) and working (green), even when collapsed.
  • Filter: All / Waiting / Working at the top of the sidebar.
  • ⌘J jumps to the next session waiting for you.

Terminal

  • ⌘-click a bare file name like [file] promo.mp4 or README.md: ClaudeDeck finds it in the session's folder, in the files Claude recently wrote or sent in that session, or elsewhere in the project, and shows it in Finder (⌘⌥-click opens it).

Installed 0.2.0? This update arrives through ClaudeDeck › Check for Updates… (or on its own within a day).

item.title: ClaudeDeck 0.2.0
item.description:
ClaudeDeck 0.2.0 turns the deck into a place where you can also read, review and ship the code your Claude sessions write — without leaving the window.

New

  • Tabs in the main window. Files, full-width diffs and Automations open as tabs in the toolbar; Sessions is always the first tab. Preview tabs (italic) are replaced by the next file you open until you edit or pin them. ⌘1–⌘9 and ⌃Tab switch tabs, drag to reorder, right-click for Close Others / Open in Separate Window. Prefer windows? Settings › open files in separate windows.
  • Built-in editor. Light code editor with syntax highlighting, find & replace, ⌘S, reload when the file changes on disk, and Add to Claude that inserts @path#L10-20 for the selected lines.
  • Changes (⌘⇧G). Source control in the right panel: stage, unstage or discard per file or per hunk, commit / amend / push / pull, ✨ generate the commit message with your own claude, and Ask Claude about this line… from any diff line.
  • Explorer upgrades. Live file tree (including external commits), respects .gitignore, Quick Open (⌘P), Find in Files (⌘⇧F), cut / copy / paste / duplicate, drag to move, drop files from Finder.
  • GitHub issues & pull requests. Link one to a session and its badge shows the state; the popover has CI checks, reviews and the latest comments, plus Add Comment and Send to Claude. You get notified on a new review, a failing check or a merge. Uses your own gh CLI — ClaudeDeck stores no tokens.
  • Automations. Saved prompts that start a Claude session hourly, daily, on weekdays or weekly (or on demand with Run Now), in the project folder or a fresh git worktree, with run history and templates. They run while ClaudeDeck is running (menu bar mode + open at login keep it alive).
  • Restart Session (⌘⌥R) and Restart All Claude Sessions. Quits claude and resumes the same conversation, so newly added MCP servers and settings are picked up with one click.
  • Pencil (pen.dev) integration. Claude sessions started by ClaudeDeck get the Pencil desktop app's MCP server automatically, and .pen files open in Pencil. Optional; off when Pencil isn't installed.
  • ⌘-click paths and links in the terminal. A file path Claude prints (like promo-video/out/promo.mp4 or src/app.ts:42) is resolved against the session's project folder and shown in Finder; ⌘⌥-click opens the file itself. URLs open in the browser.
  • Automatic updates. ClaudeDeck now checks for new versions at launch and daily and installs them for you (Sparkle, signed updates). ClaudeDeck › Check for Updates… checks on demand. If an update is waiting at launch, your sessions start after you decide, so installing it doesn't restart them twice.
  • Interrupted sessions always pick up where they left off. A session that was working when ClaudeDeck quit — or crashed — gets "Continue where you left off." when it comes back. Idle sessions simply resume; sending the message to every session is optional. The automatic /compact after a resume is now off by default.
  • Copy Path in the project context menu.

Notes

  • Coming from 0.1.0: 0.1.0 has no updater, so install 0.2.0 by hand once (download the DMG below and replace the app). From 0.2.0 on, updates arrive automatically.
  • Requires macOS 15 or later. gh (for GitHub linking) and Pencil are optional.
  • Your data file gains new fields (automations, GitHub links, new settings). Going back to 0.1.0 afterwards works, but 0.1.0 drops those fields the next time it saves.
